howTo: Enter the design shear/tension force (F) in Newtons (N), the total effective weld length (L) in millimeters (mm), and the allowable weld shear stress (σ_allow or τ_allow) in MPa (N/mm²).
If sizing a new joint, leave fillet leg size (a) empty or 0 to compute the minimum required leg length and throat thickness.
If checking an existing weld, enter the specified leg size (a) in millimeters to evaluate calculated throat stress against allowable stress.
formula: a_req = F / (0.707 · L · σ_allow) | throat = 0.707 · a | τ_throat = F / (0.707 · a · L)

examples.title: Required leg size calculation (sizing mode)
examples.description: F = 15 kN static load, L = 120 mm total effective length, allowable weld shear stress σ_allow = 140 MPa.
notes: In production, round up the required 1.26 mm leg size to the minimum practical weld size (typically 3 mm or 4 mm based on plate thickness requirements).
Effective weld length excludes start and stop end craters (deduct 2 · a from physical run length if no run-on/run-off tabs are used).

examples.title: Existing weld verification (stress check mode)
examples.description: F = 20 kN static load, L = 150 mm, allowable stress = 160 MPa, existing leg size a = 6 mm.
notes: Calculated throat shear stress is 31.43 MPa, well below allowable 160 MPa (utilization ratio ≈ 19.6%).
Assumes equal load distribution across the 150 mm joint without out-of-plane peel or tearing moments.

references.title: AWS D1.1 / D1.1M (Structural Welding Code — Steel)
references.note: Section 2.4/2.5 covering effective throat dimensioning (t_e = 0.707 · w) for equal-leg 45° fillet welds under simplified static shear analysis.

references.title: EN 1993-1-8 (Eurocode 3: Design of steel structures — Design of joints)
references.note: Section 4.5.3.3 covering the simplified method for design resistance of fillet welds where resultant force is transferred through the throat area.

references.title: Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design
references.note: Chapter on welded joints in tension, compression, and shear. Basis for the simplified throat shear stress approximation.

commonMistakes: Entering total physical bead length without deducting start and crater end run-off lengths (effective length L_eff = L_total − 2·a).
Confusing fillet leg length (a or w) with throat thickness (throat = 0.707·a). Note that Eurocode 3 designates throat thickness as 'a' whereas American textbooks designate leg length as 'a' or 'w'.
Using material ultimate tensile strength (Rm) or yield strength (Re) directly as allowable stress instead of applying appropriate joint efficiency and safety factors.
assumptions: Equal-leg 45° fillet weld profile: the effective throat thickness is taken as the theoretical throat t = a · cos(45°) ≈ 0.707 · a.
Simplified shear method: the applied resultant load is assumed uniformly distributed as pure shear across the minimum throat plane, regardless of load orientation.
Static loading only: dynamic fatigue cyclic reversal, residual thermal stresses, and weld metal toughness factors are omitted.
Zero load eccentricity: out-of-plane bending, peel stresses, and secondary moments on the connection are neglected.

Preliminary engineering screening: this simplified tool does not substitute for licensed structural joint verification under full directional methods (e.g. AWS D1.1 directional factor or EN 1993-1-8 directional formulation with β_w and γ_M2).
